context: B2.3 (Podman GPU passthrough probe) was sealed in acceptance/W0.json with result=deferred per ADR 0007 §GPU passthrough deferral, pending post-reboot validation. This amendment records the post-reboot validation outcome as a separate, fresh artifact. Sealed acceptance/W0.json and audit/W0.json are not modified; the deferred result in the sealed acceptance archive is not retroactively re-classified. This amendment is a forward-pointing addendum, not a re-seal.

acceptance_archive.b2_3_disposition_in_archive: result=deferred per ADR 0007 §GPU passthrough deferral; post-reboot validation scheduled for Sunday post-SF-queue per Kyle

audit_archive.b2_3_disposition_in_archive: AF003 (important) — deferral acceptable for 0.2.17 W0/W3 (hybrid mode uses host); gates 0.3.x production readiness

verification_sequence.evidence: NVML init clean post-reboot. All 595.71.05 libs resolved. /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml written with CDI spec version 0.5.0. Expected warnings only (libnvidia-vulkan-producer, X11 confs, nvidia-imex — all optional and not present on this desktop install).
Container saw RTX 2080 SUPER, driver 595.71.05, 51MiB/8192MiB, P8 idle. Same GPU state as host nvidia-smi.
verification_sequence.tag_drift_note: Original B2.3 plan-text and ADR 0007 §GPU passthrough deferral validation-path snippet referenced docker.io/nvidia/cuda:12.0-base, which has been retired in NVIDIA's docker.io tag scheme. Current scheme is 12.x.y-base-ubuntu24.04 family. Validation used 12.6.3-base-ubuntu24.04 as the verified-current tag at validation time. Tag drift recorded as F-0.2.17-W0-005 in carry-forwards-0.2.16.md (deployment-doc lesson — pre-flight automation should query current tag set at runtime or pin to verified-current tags).

outcome.host_state_post_reboot: userspace 595.71.05 + kernel module 595.71.05 (mismatch resolved); NVML init clean
outcome.host_native_ollama_path_unchanged: ADR 0008 hybrid-mode dispatcher continues to route to host's native Ollama; this amendment does not alter that wire. Container GPU passthrough now also available for any future workload that needs to run inside the container against the GPU.
